rows.heading: ## Restore discipline — before/after identity, not continuous non-write proof
rows.claim: **All edits in scratch:** `cp -p` the artifact into the lane namespace and edit only copies
rows.excerpt: Substrate: kumitate-shokunin **read-only** — every mutant is a copy under `/tmp/tameshi-r2-1-work/`, and no fleet file was written.
rows.note: The pointed lines support the clause's scratch half ('every mutant is a copy under `/tmp/tameshi-r2-1-work/`, and no fleet file was written') but carry no `cp -p`: `git -C LANE show BASE:corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kimi-census.md | grep -n 'cp -p'` prints only :172, and :150 calls the scratch file a 'byte-copy'. The clause names `cp -p` as the copy mechanism - the flag that preserves mtime for the step-3 endpoint proof - so :4-7 does not support the clause it is attached to. Two earlier cold reads found the same aim: .ufo/waves/round-17/w2/CR10.md:84-87 ('item 2's kimi anchor is indirect ... the literal `cp -p` command is at §4:172') and .ufo/waves/round-29/w1/Read02C.md:7 ('the literal `cp -p` command in that note is at :172'). No line drift (single addition at 2587e0a). Repair keeps one pointer: `mutation-case-kimi-census.md:4-7, :172`, ranges [[4,7],[172,172]], verified with the counter's own pointed_text - the scratch sentence and `cp -p kumitate-shokunin/scripts/kimi-census.mjs /tmp/tameshi-r2-1-work/pristine.mjs` are both inside it. Shown by: git -C LANE show BASE:corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kimi-census.md | sed -n '4,7p;172p'.

proposed_fix.why: The clause prescribes `cp -p` (mtime-preserving copy); the base range :4-7 carries only the read-only-substrate sentence, and the note's literal `cp -p` is at :172. Extending to :4-7, :172 keeps one pointer (section floor 10), fixes the aim, and leaves both halves located; the row must then be re-keyed on raw 'mutation-case-kimi-census.md:4-7, :172' with ranges [[4,7],[172,172]].
